query: Many physical and chemical fabrication approaches have produced multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles, yet their synthesis–structure–property relationships remain poorly established. This limits evaluation of their suitability for catalytic operation at 773–1173 K and thermoelectric use at 473–1923 K, including catalytic settings where low noble-metal content is desirable. What governs whether these nanoparticles preserve structural and chemical stability under such service regimes, and why? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, specify a controlled intervention that separates it from competing explanations, predict observations relative to a baseline, define its boundary conditions, connect it to the prior evidence summarized above, and provide a clear falsification test.

generation.hypothesis: The preservation of structural and chemical stability in near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles under high-temperature service regimes is governed by the optimization of their surface energy and grain boundary composition.
generation.material_initial_state: Near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles with varying surface energies and grain boundary compositions
generation.intervention: Controlled annealing treatments at temperatures between 773-1173 K to alter grain boundary composition and surface energy
generation.conditions: High-temperature service regimes (773-1173 K for catalytic operation and 473-1923 K for thermoelectric use)
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary composition and surface energy
generation.mechanism: Optimization of surface energy and grain boundary composition leads to enhanced structural and chemical stability
generation.predicted_outcome: Nanoparticles with optimized surface energy and grain boundary composition will exhibit improved structural and chemical stability under high-temperature service regimes compared to those without optimization
generation.baseline: Nanoparticles without optimized surface energy and grain boundary composition
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 773-1173 K for catalytic operation and 473-1923 K for thermoelectric use
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between surface energy, grain boundary composition, and structural/chemical stability is not well established

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of nanoparticles with varying surface energies and grain boundary compositions under controlled high-temperature service regimes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If nanoparticles with optimized surface energy and grain boundary composition do not exhibit improved structural and chemical stability under high-temperature service regimes, the hypothesis is falsified
